text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: auth-service | spike in 401s (external) starting 2026-03-18T12:07Z. alert threshold crossed (5x baseline). sample log: `2026-03-18T12:07:21Z auth[svc]: 401 Authorization failed for token=ghp_*** fragment=...`

olivia: oncall ack — i'll take lead. starting triage.

raj: seeing concentrated traffic from 3 ipv4 blocks located in EU region. user-agent looks like generic crawler. rate per ip ~120r/s.

marta: CS note: three customers reported auth failures in EU-1 (acme-corp, papertrail, betainc). acme reports ~10% of requests failing.

tim: i can push a temporary WAF ip block and reduce bot traffic. will also enable tighter rate-limits on /v1/auth/introspect.

olivia: good. preserve logs first. @incident-bot please create incident ticket and snapshot logs.

incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-4723. Saved logs to s3://redwood-incident-archive/4812349999/ (preserve=true).

raj: no prod deploys to auth in last 6h. telemetry suggests token replay / credential stuffing rather than app bug.

olivia: tim, apply WAF ip block and add a short-term rule to reject requests with malformed auth headers. keep me posted.

tim: executing now. command: ```bash
aws wafv2 update-ip-set --name "incident-block-4812349999" --scope REGIONAL --addresses 203.0.113.0/24 198.51.100.0/24 192.0.2.0/24
```

tim: rule applied, 3 ip blocks blocked. traffic from those IPs dropped to 0. monitoring for fallback. :thumbsup: 

marta: CS update posted to INC-2026-4723: acme-corp impacted, severity assessed as S2. notifying account owners and offering temporary workaround (increase retries + backoff).

amy: customer-success here — i've emailed affected customers with workaround + ETA. draft comms in ticket. no customer escalations yet.

raj: while triaging found a separate concern: our log-forwarder on a staging cluster was misconfigured and forwarded debug logs that include partial auth fragments to an external indexer last night. sounds like staging only but need to confirm scope.

olivia: that's high risk. marta/tim, pls confirm whether any prod indexers received forwarded logs. if any tokens were exposed we need to rotate. jordan (legal) joining.

tim: searching forwarding configs and recipients — running grep across hosts now. snippet used for search: ```bash
grep -R "forwarder\.external" /etc/logshipper || true
```

tim: preserved live-forwarder configs to s3://redwood-incident-archive/4812349999/configs/ and disabled external forwarders on staging.

raj: quick token-scan across preserved logs: ```bash
zcat /var/log/auth/*.gz | egrep -i "(Authorization:|token=|Bearer )" | head -n 50
```

raj: initial pass: a handful of PARTIAL token fragments found in staging debug logs only. no full tokens captured for prod services so far.

olivia: good. still treat as sensitive. action list: 1) maintain WAF blocks 2) preserve all related logs 3) inventory svc accounts touched by potential fragments 4) rotate keys for any exposed svc accounts 5) decide if KMS key rotation needed for affected resources 6) customer comms + legal notification.

marta: prepping rotation runbook for svc-acct list; will stage rotation times and coordinate with customers if their integrations are affected.

jordan: legal — if any customer-identifiable data or PHI is in forwarded logs, we need timeline and scope within 24h. keep legal looped in INC-2026-4723.

tim: i created a preserved snapshot of prod auth logs and configuration: s3://redwood-incident-archive/4812349999/prod-snapshot.tar.gz (access=restricted). masking rules applied to archived artifacts.

raj: running automated sweep to identify tokens / credentials in archived data. command: ```bash
python tools/find_secrets.py --paths s3://redwood-incident-archive/4812349999 --pattern "Authorization|Bearer|token=" --output results/4812349999-findings.json
```

raj: if findings > 0 we'll pivot to immediate rotate for those specific keys.

amy: customers notified about incident investigation and temporary mitigations. asked to report any anomalous errors.

olivia: decision checkpoint: current mitigation (WAF + rate-limit) reduced external 401 flood by ~95%. no confirmed prod key exfiltration. proceed with targeted svc-acct rotations only if findings surface. keep legal and CS updated.

marta: i'll start pre-rotations for low-risk service accounts (non-customer-facing) to be ready if needed.

tim: added a temporary monitoring alert to detect any auth-header pattern changes and raised sampling to 10x for EU region for next 2 hours.

olivia: thanks team. please post short updates to INC-2026-4723 every 30m or on any material change. we'll leave the page open for 2 hours then reassess.

incident-bot: PAGER STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. incident state updated to "mitigated" in INC-2026-4723.

olivia: :lock: closing note — if scans find exposed full tokens, escalate to immediate full key rotation + KMS rotation plan. otherwise continue monitoring and preserve evidence for 7 days.

tim: :thumbsup: will keep watch and revert if anything changes.
